question_text: What is a differential signal pair, and why is it preferred over single-ended signals for high-speed routing (like USB or Ethernet)?
answer_text: A differential pair uses two traces to transmit equal and opposite (inverted) signals. The receiver reads the difference between them, making it highly immune to common-mode noise.
explanation_text: If external electromagnetic interference (EMI) hits the routing, it couples into both parallel traces equally. Because the receiver only cares about the mathematical difference between the two voltages, this "common-mode" noise gets completely cancelled out.
bonus_question_text: Do differential pairs emit less EMI than single-ended traces?
bonus_answer_text: Yes. Because the currents on the two traces are equal and opposite, their radiated magnetic fields effectively cancel each other out.
